holdings: Section IV explains Copyright Act 37: scope fixed by agreement; unclear scope presumed unlicensed; exclusive licensee can exercise rights and litigate in own name within scope while original rightsholder cannot exercise them within that scope.

The lower court interpreted the Korean publisher's 2011 Taiwan exclusive distribution agreement together with a 2014 copyright license as granting exclusive copyright permission. Supreme Court found the challenged evidentiary reasoning insufficient to establish a qualifying error of law.

Different Korean/Chinese document dates were addressed through evidence that a lost Korean original was reproduced in 2018, the 2014 Chinese agreement, Korean notarization and Taipei representative-office authentication. This is a case-specific evidentiary explanation, not a rule that date discrepancies do not matter.
limits: Distribution exclusivity is not automatically an exclusive copyright license.
License is not an assignment of copyright ownership.
No claim about current Korean copyright law, no invented firm involvement.

holdings: Section VI(1)1: genuine goods sold by or with consent of the same global trademark owner attract international exhaustion, but this does not automatically authorize separate service-source signage and advertising.
Brand-dominant counter/window/outlet-website displays, less prominent reseller identification/parallel-import wording and presentation as a branded outlet supported infringement findings.
Nominative fair use must be assessed case by case; honest necessary identification can be lawful. This case does not prohibit every advertisement for genuine goods.
Outlet operator's advertising control, revenue share, actual awareness and continuation after notices matter; it was not treated merely as a passive landlord.

sources.outcome: Employee's partial appeal dismissed; first instance awarded TWD9,467 plus interest, rejected the balance; additional TWD1,090,460 sought on appeal rejected.
sources.stage: Appeal from 臺灣橋頭地方法院113年度勞訴字第44號 (2025-05-27). Judgment expressly says 本判決不得上訴.
sources.finality_limit: Ordinary appeal unavailable by judgment's own notice; do not claim no extraordinary remedy could ever exist.
holdings: Section III identifies which portions were appealed: holiday pay TWD154,287 and time-barred overtime TWD225,249 were not appealed and were already final.
Section VI(1): employee signed contemporaneous confirmations marking differences in clock times as non-overtime; allegations of collusion/coercion were not proved on the evidence.

Section VI(2): court acknowledged Labor Incident Act38 presumption, considered actual approval/confirmation practices and lack of additional positive evidence. Some dates without non-overtime confirmations had already supported an award.
Section VI(3): the particular after-hours chat extracts were mutual reminders of work matters and did not establish work performed in this case.
limits: Not every after-hours message is unpaid; not every late clock-out establishes overtime.
A written application system alone is not a universal defense.
Do not recommend coercing employees to sign non-overtime confirmations or describe managers as automatically exempt.
Hotel chef facts are not facts about the Korean AE job posting.

sources.court: 臺灣臺北地方法院臺北簡易庭
sources.read_coverage: Official 90-line page opened, turn971view1 lines0-46 including complete substantive reasons through Civil Code130/144. Last lines47-89 not retrieved on reopen. Official indexed text turn1091search0 confirms claims/facts/reasons; turn1077search1 gives small-claims legal-error appeal notice. Do NOT label full-text read complete.
sources.outcome: Traveler's TWD55,150 refund suit dismissed on limitation defense; TWD1,500 costs borne by claimant.
sources.stage: Small-claims first instance; ordinary limited appeal route mentioned in official indexed notice; appeal history/finality not verified.
holdings: Tour should have ended 2024-04-02; one-year deadline was 2025-04-02 under Civil Code514-12; suit filed 2025-10-09.
2024-05-27 complaint/unsuccessful industry-association handling did not preserve interruption: no suit within six months of demand, so Civil Code130 treated that demand-based interruption as absent.
Defendant raised limitation defense and could refuse performance under144(1).
limits: The dispute concerned a Taiwan tour operator's outbound Iceland/Paris package with self-booked flights, not a Korean tourist's Taiwan inbound tour.
Do not say court validated the operator's 100% cancellation charge; that was an argument, while dismissal rested on time bar.
One-year rule is for claims in the Civil Code tourism section, not every hotel/airline/platform refund.
Industry-association 調處 is not interchangeable with statutory court 調解; other procedures may have different effects.
Six months from a demand is not an automatic universal refund-suit deadline; calculate the underlying one-year period and any effective interruption separately.
